title: Chat assignment
description: What the hub tells the connector about one chat: its scope, whether its daemon should run, whether an agent session is wanted and how, and the origins the hub minted for it (their port rule is C-06.29a, A-06.2). Contract 05 carries this object as the body of its assignment message; this schema is the body only. The connector applies assignments per chat in rev order and ignores a rev it has already applied.

chat_id.description: The chat label (contract 03 section 2): the chat id without its cht_ prefix, as every 05 frame names a chat and as the chat-<label> origins carry it.

rev.description: Monotonic per chat. A rev at or below the last applied one is ignored.

issued_at.description: When the hub issued this revision, epoch ms (information only; ordering is rev).

title.description: The chat's display name, for the connector's log and `connect status`. Never written into the root.

scope.description: Where the chat's files are. A folder chat names an offered folder by id only; a repo chat is cloned by the connector; a space chat gets an empty directory.

folder_id.description: The offered folder's id (06-connector-state.json#/$defs/folder). Never a path.

kind.description: A GitHub clone the connector makes under its workdir.

url.description: https clone URL with no credentials in it; the clone uses the machine's own git credentials.

ref.description: Branch or tag to check out; the default branch when absent. Never starts with -: the connector also refuses such a ref before git runs (C-06.16), so it cannot be read as an option.

kind.description: The chat's own space: an empty directory under the connector's workdir.

desired.description: running: the daemon is up and held up (the retain stream); stopped: the hold is released (or the daemon shut down, see stop_mode); removed: stopped, then the mapping is forgotten. Owned roots stay on disk in v1.

stop_mode.description: With desired stopped or removed. release (the default): drop the hold and let the daemon's idle grace end it; now: POST /api/shutdown, only on a daemon the connector started.

agent.description: The Claude Code session beside the daemon.

want.description: none: a surface only (it does not count against the cap); session: the chat should have an agent.

launch.description: manual: the user starts the session at the machine (`claude-web-chat connect attach <chat-label>`); connector: the connector launches it under tmux (needs let_home_start_agents, the cap, tmux, and one prior manual attach in the root, else needs-trust; C-06.26).

requested_by.description: Who asked for the session: the user, or Home on the user's behalf. Shown in status and logs.

origins.description: The origins the hub minted for this chat. The connector uses them for the answer-origin header, frame-ancestors and the X-WC-Embed-Parent response header on the relayed health (C-06.31, C-06.33), verbatim, port included; it never derives them itself. The three carry the same port or none: the port of the hub's public origin exactly when that origin carries one, 1 to 65535 with no leading zero, never 443 (C-06.29a, A-06.2). The host parts are unchanged: chat-<label>.<host>, chat-<label>-a.<host> and <host>.

surface.description: The surface endpoint, https://chat-<label>.<hub>, with :<port> after the host exactly when the hub's public origin carries one (C-06.29a, A-06.2).

answer.description: The answer origin, https://chat-<label>-a.<hub>, with the surface's port or none (C-06.29a, A-06.2).

shell.description: The hub shell's origin that frames the surface; becomes the X-WC-Embed-Parent response header on the relayed GET /api/health (C-06.33) and the extra frame-ancestors source (C-06.31). Its port, or none, is the surface's and the answer's (C-06.29a, A-06.2).
